extracted.intended_audience: Catholic faithful and clergy in Czechoslovakia (readers of the newspaper)
extracted.subtask_description: A published pastoral letter (June 1949) from the Czechoslovak Catholic hierarchy describing state measures against the Church and listing conditions the Government must meet for a just church–state agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of the Christian world view in public life and education
rubrics_metrics.description: The Christian world viewpoint (philosophy) will be recognized and respected in public life and education, in word and deed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as Condition 1 for any agreement; the bishops require positive legal and social respect for Christianity's place in public life and schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government recognition of the Pope's spiritual authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government recognizes the spiritual authority of the Roman Pope as the supreme head of the church in matters religious and ecclesiastical, which does not touch the sovereignty of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition 2 for agreement; framed as compatible with state sovereignty and grounded in freedom of religion and human rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of measures restricting religious freedom and youth education before negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the beginning of negotiations, all measures restricting and threatening religious freedom of Catholics in the Czechoslovak Republic, especially the religious freedom and education of youth, be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition 3 for agreement; the bishops insist restrictions be undone as a precondition to meaningful talks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit ecclesiastical gazettes and publishing free of state control (Gazette of the Catholic Clergy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gazette of the Catholic Clergy (published by the Ministry) will be published immediately, and the publishing of all official dignitaries' gazettes will be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (a) appended to the main conditions; criticized earlier where the Ministry published a gazette 'which has no church endorsement and is edited against the will of the hierarchy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Revoke specific anti-church decrees (vacant offices, assembly restrictions, security procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decree of the Ministry of Education, Arts and Sciences of May 23, 1949 (about vacant church offices and accompanying stipends), as well as the decree of the Ministry of Interior of May 5, 1949 (restricting freedom of assembly and congregation), and the decree for regional and district command of the state security police on procedure against the Catholic Church, must be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition (b) appended to the main conditions; these concrete legal instruments are named as requiring revocation before negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of all restrictions involving religious rights
rubrics_metrics.description: All restrictions involving the religious rights must be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An additional demand appended to the main conditions; emphasized as necessary so the Church 'would be able to fulfill its spiritual mission—that is, to teach, to sanctify and to direct.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No state censorship of Catholic books and prayer books
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Catholic book that is to be published—even prayer books—should not be subjected to preliminary state censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter condemns 'Every Catholic book... subjected to preliminary state censorship' and presents freedom of Catholic publishing as essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: No state agents or plenipotentiaries in Catholic publishing houses
rubrics_metrics.description: State plenipotentiaries must not be planted in Catholic publishing houses or otherwise control church publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops cite the placement of state agents in publishing houses as an attempt to govern ecclesiastical affairs 'wholly ecclesiastical' and exclude bishops from their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of ecclesiastical press and authenticity of official church gazettes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ecclesiastical press and the official gazettes of the Bishops must be allowed to operate; publications directed by the State without church endorsement are not truly ecclesiastical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter notes 'All the ecclesiastical press... has been stopped' and criticizes the Ministry's Gazette of the Catholic Clergy as 'directed by non-Catholics in an anti-church spirit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of assembly and schooling for Catholics outside churches
rubrics_metrics.description: No interdiction of assembly and schooling of Catholics outside churches should be imposed under threat of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter documents interdictions 'edited under the threat of prosecution' and lists repeal of such measures among bargaining conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of church buildings, ritual objects, and property from illegal inventory and seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: Church buildings, ritual objects, sacred vessels, collections and other church property must not be subjected to forced inventories, illegal searches, seizures, or deprivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops describe 'forced inventory of ritual objects and sacred vessels' and 'anti-constitutional searches' and warn the church is 'deprived of the last remnants of its property.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference with monastic houses and institutions for clerical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to deprive church buildings of their religious missions—especially by taking over monasteries and institutions for the education of clerical and monastic youth—must cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter gives examples, notably in Slovakia where 'some monastic houses were forcibly cleared out and the priests taken away in trucks.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption and payment of state stipends to priests
rubrics_metrics.description: The paying of the state stipend of priests should not be stopped and must be resumed where halted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops note that in many cases 'the paying of the state stipend of priests was stopped,' causing suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and security of church schools and religious education
rubrics_metrics.description: Church schools must be allowed to exist and be secure; religious education of youth in schools and extra-curricular settings must be possible and not rendered illegal by state monopolies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter states 'Church schools practically no longer exist' and criticizes a state monopoly on 'materialist school and extra-curricular education' that makes Christian education impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious teachers must not be ideologically tested or forced to teach materialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers of religion should not be tested ideologically nor required to teach religion 'in the materialistic spirit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops condemn ideological testing and directives intended to produce materialistic instruction even in theological contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theological education must be free from materialist social-science indoctrination
rubrics_metrics.description: Theological schools should not institute courses in social science with the aim that 'even theological students should be educated in the materialistic ideology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter describes such courses being introduced to bring theological students under materialist influence; this is presented as unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No illegal searches or inspections of church property
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventories and inspections of church property must be carried out lawfully; illegal 'direct inspection' and 'anti-constitutional searches' are condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops report ordered inventories 'quite illegally' with 'direct inspection' and label them anti-constitutional.

rubrics_metrics.name: No state surveillance, occupation, or listening devices in ecclesiastical meetings/offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Police occupation of church offices, surveillance of bishops' conferences, and use of listening devices are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter recounts discovery of listening devices in the Bishops' conference room and 'Police Occupy Consistory,' presenting these as extreme breaches of constitutional freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to practice rites and hold religious processions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practicing of religious rites must not be forbidden and religious processions must not be made impossible or misused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops note in some places 'the practicing of religious rites has already been forbidden' and that processions were 'made impossible or were misused for irreligious purposes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: State should not instruct security forces to suppress church and members
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministry of Interior or other state organs must not issue instructions to state security/police on how to deal with the church and its members in a suppressive manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter records that the Ministry of Interior 'gave instructions to the regional command of the state security [police] on how to deal with the church and its members.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect constitutional freedoms and existing laws in dealings with the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions imposed on the Church that breach constitutional freedoms and 'many of the still-existent laws' must be ended; government actions should conform to the constitution and law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops repeatedly characterize state measures as 'extreme breaches of constitutional freedoms' and illegal under current laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government must not create or sponsor a pseudo-‘Catholic Action’ hostile to hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will not support or grant state sponsorship to the newly formed, regime-backed 'Catholic Action' which lacks bishops' endorsement and is aimed to hinder episcopal authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops denounce the meeting of a government-prepared 'Catholic Action' (June 10, 1949) convened 'without the knowledge of and against the will of the Bishops' and declare participation in such action forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church disciplinary rule: founding or participating in so‑called action committees is forbidden
rubrics_metrics.description: Every attempt at founding diocese, regional, district or parish so‑called action committees is forbidden by the Church; clergymen and laymen who participate or accept functions in them will be excommunicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bench of Bishops declared the so‑called Catholic Action 'not Catholic' and stated that 'the inspirators have... been excommunicated' pursuant to Canon law (Canon 2334, Paragraph 2 and Canon 2231, Paragraph 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clergy must obey only legitimately published ecclesiastical directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Directives published by consistories under Government control are not ecclesiastically binding; clergy are bound by conscience to observe only those directives they are safely convinced were published by their respective dignitaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit pastoral instruction: clergy should not take as binding any directives that originate from government-controlled or illegitimate sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bishops assert loyalty to the republic while reserving right to defend Church rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bishops declare they 'were always loyal to the republic' (oath upon taking office) and require clergy to refrain from political activity, yet they will rightfully defend the rights of the Holy Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to counter claims that bishops were disloyal; frames permissible behavior (no illegal political activity) and the bishops' duty to protect church rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priests must read and inform faithful of the pastoral letter; failure penalized
rubrics_metrics.description: This pastoral letter 'is to be read in all parish churches and chapels at public services' on a specified date; 'Willful and intentional neglect of this duty will be prosecuted with ecclesiastical punishment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction to clergy to inform the faithful openly of the state of affairs; framed as an obligatory pastoral duty with canonical consequences for neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pastoral guidance to the faithful: remain loyal, avoid provocation, pray
rubrics_metrics.description: The faithful are exhorted to 'remain loyal to your Bishops,' strengthen the Church by prayer, Christian life and 'unconditional loyalty,' to not be misled by false prophets, and to avoid unmeditated and provocative actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and prudential guidance during persecution: spiritual endurance, non-violent steadfastness, and adherence to Church authority are emphasized as proper responses.
